description: One person this employer has authorised to complete and sign a federal employment form on its behalf — Section 2 of Form I-9, the Employers Only block of Form W-4, or both. A child table on I-9 Settings rather than a doctype of its own because the roster has no existence apart from the site it belongs to and is read on every signature, and because a second Single holding six columns is table sprawl. WHO SIGNS IS NOT WHO CALLS. The row names the person whose name goes on the form; the account that made the call is on the I-9 Audit Log row regardless, and the two are different facts. A site with no rows at all is not policed — that is the pre-v0.48.0 behaviour and it is what an install does before anybody has configured anything.

fields.description: The account this authorisation belongs to. It is what the signature check matches on, so an account that is not here signs nothing once the roster has a single row in it.
fields.label: User

fields.description: The printed name as it should appear on the form — the name a federal inspector reads, not the account's login. 'Ana Ramos', not 'ana@example.com'.
fields.label: Full Name

fields.description: Job title as it goes on the form. Form I-9 asks for it in the same box as the name; Form W-4 does not print it, and it is recorded on the W-4 anyway so the record says who processed the form.
fields.label: Title

fields.description: May complete and sign Section 2 of Form I-9 — the attestation that this person personally examined the employee's documents.
fields.label: Can Sign I-9

fields.description: May complete the Employers Only block of Form W-4.
fields.label: Can Sign W-4

fields.description: Off means this person no longer signs. THE ROW STAYS — remove_authorized_signer clears this flag rather than deleting, because a form signed in 2026 was signed by whoever was authorised in 2026 and a deleted row makes that unanswerable.
fields.label: Active

name: Authorized Signer
